<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
The integral equations \eqref{j1-int-eqn} and \eqref{int-eqn} admit unique continuous solutions $\tilde{j}_n(\xi,t)$ in $[0,T]$ for each $\xi$ for $\tilde{d}(\xi,t)$ that is continuous in $t$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
For Drude weight perturbation $d(x,t)$ in $L^2((0,t),H^1(\mathbb{R}))$, the perturbational corrections $\tilde{j}_n(\xi,t)$ for $n=1,2,\dots$ have Fourier inverses for finite $t$ and are in $L^2((0,t),L^2(\mathbb{R}))$.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
